title: Why Two-Step Transition Probabilities Form P²
text:
Let (P) be the transition matrix of a Markov chain.
Why does the ((i,j))-entry of (P^2) represent the probability of moving from state (i) to state (j) in two steps?

title: Why Two-Step Transition Probabilities Form P²
text:
One-step transition probabilities
The one-step transition probability is defined by
\[
p(i,j)
=
P(X_{n+1}=j \mid X_n=i).
\]
This is the probability that the chain moves from state (i) to state (j) in one step.

title: Why Two-Step Transition Probabilities Form P²
text:
Two-step transition probabilities
Suppose that the chain begins at state (i) and reaches state (j) after two steps.
At the intermediate step, the chain may visit any state (k). Therefore,
\[
P(X_{n+2}=j \mid X_n=i)
=
\sum_{k\in S}
P(X_{n+2}=j, X_{n+1}=k \mid X_n=i).
\]
Using the Markov property,
\[
P(X_{n+2}=j \mid X_{n+1}=k, X_n=i)
=
P(X_{n+2}=j \mid X_{n+1}=k).
\]
Hence,
\[
p^{(2)}(i,j)
=
\sum_{k\in S}p(i,k)p(k,j).
\]

title: Why Two-Step Transition Probabilities Form P²
text:
Connection with matrix multiplication
By the definition of matrix multiplication,
\[
(P^2)_{ij}
=
\sum_{k\in S}P_{ik}P_{kj}.
\]
Since (P_{ik}=p(i,k)) and (P_{kj}=p(k,j)), we obtain
\[
\boxed{p^{(2)}(i,j)=(P^2)_{ij}}.
\]

title: Why Two-Step Transition Probabilities Form P²
text:
Intuition
Each term
\[
p(i,k)p(k,j)
\]
is the probability of following the particular path
\[
i \longrightarrow k \longrightarrow j.
\]
Because the intermediate state (k) can be any state, we add the probabilities of all possible two-step paths.

title: Understanding Transition Probabilities
text:
Interpretation
The quantity (p(i,j)) represents the probability that the chain moves to state (j) at the next step, given that its current state is (i).
